hints.content: The International Space Station reaches its perigee every time $A(t)$ reaches its minimum.

$A(t)$ will reach its minimum whenever 

$\sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi (t+23.2)}{92.8}\right)$

reaches its maximum. That happens when $\dfrac{2\pi (t+23.2)}{92.8}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ plus a multiple of $2\pi$.

We can solve that equation:

$\begin{align}
\dfrac{2\pi (t+23.2)}{92.8} &= \frac{\pi}{2} + 2\pi n \\
\\
t + 23.2 &=  23.2 + 92.8 n \\
\\
t &=  92.8 n. \\
\end{align}$

The ISS is at its perigee whenever $t$ is a multiple of $92.8$ minutes. That happens every $92.8$ minutes.
Since the ISS reaches its perigee once in every orbit, it takes $92.8$ minutes to orbit the earth.

question.content:
The altitude of the International Space Station $t$ minutes after its perigee (closest point), in kilometers, is given by

$\qquad A(t) = 415 - \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi (t + 23.2)}{92.8}\right)$.

The International Space Station reaches its perigee once in every orbit.

**How long does the International Space Station take to orbit the earth? Give an exact answer.**

[[☃ input-number 1]] minutes
